papers.title: Molecular determinants of ligand recognition and efficacy in the TRPM3 voltage sensor-like domain.
papers.abstract: Transient receptor potential melastatin 3 (TRPM3) is a calcium-permeable ion channel implicated in chronic pain and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. The voltage sensor-like domain (VSLD) is a major site of pharmacological modulation, but the molecular determinants of ligand recognition and efficacy remain incompletely understood. Here we combine cryo-electron microscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, mutagenesis, and medicinal chemistry to investigate the interactions of TRPM3 with the inhibitors isosakuranetin, maprotiline, and diclofenac. We show that structurally diverse liga
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study combines cryo-EM, molecular dynamics, mutagenesis, and medicinal chemistry to map how three structurally diverse inhibitors (isosakuranetin, maprotiline, diclofenac) bind the voltage sensor-like domain of the TRPM3 ion channel. The work reveals molecular determinants of ligand recognition and efficacy at this pharmacologically important site, which is linked to chronic pain and developmental epileptic encephalopathies.

papers.title: Design and Evolution of an Orthogonal HaloTag for Multiplexed Labeling in Cells.
papers.abstract: The self-labeling protein HaloTag is used to install a wide variety of functional small molecules in cells and living organisms with exquisite specificity with respect to cell type and subcellular localization. HaloTag is a core part of many biotechnology-based tools for sensing, tracking, and manipulating biological systems with a high degree of spatial and temporal control. Due to the limitations of fluorescent proteins and other self-labeling proteins, most of these tools have historically been restricted to a single channel. In this work, we used structure-guided rational design and direct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper describes the design of an orthogonal HaloTag variant that can be labeled independently from the original HaloTag, enabling simultaneous multiplexed labeling of two different protein targets in cells. Using structure-guided rational design and directed evolution, the authors created a second self-labeling tag with distinct substrate specificity, expanding the toolkit for spatial and temporal control of biological systems.

papers.title: What deep learning can and cannot (yet) do for enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Deep learning has substantially advanced structure-based enzyme design, yet reliably creating highly efficient enzymes remains out of reach. One emerging enzyme design strategy combines diffusion-based scaffold generation around active-site models with sequence design. Such structure-based approaches have expanded the accessible reaction space and enabled the emergence of enzymes with diverse catalytic functions and complex catalytic motifs. Despite notable catalytic efficiencies (kcat/KM), turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited, suggesting that current approaches typically yield tight sub
papers.summary: This review examines the current capabilities and limitations of deep learning for enzyme design, highlighting that while diffusion-based scaffold generation combined with sequence design has expanded accessible reaction space and produced enzymes with diverse catalytic functions, turnover rates (kcat) often remain limited. The authors argue that reliably creating highly efficient enzymes is still out of reach, suggesting current approaches typically yield tight substrate binding but suboptimal catalysis.

papers.title: Integrative proteomic analysis and molecular dynamics simulations of ANKLE2 reveal mechanisms of microcephaly.
papers.abstract: ANKLE2 is a scaffolding protein with crucial roles in neuroprogenitor cell division and embryonic brain development. Pathogenic variants in ANKLE2 cause primary microcephaly, a congenital disorder characterized by impaired neurodevelopment. Nonetheless, the underlying dysfunction of ANKLE2 is not understood. Here, we define the ANKLE2 protein interaction landscape, which includes cell division proteins and novel microcephaly candidates in the APC (anaphase-promoting complex). Analysis of six pathogenic variants reveals changes in this interactome that likely result in microcephaly. Using molec
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study maps the protein interaction landscape of ANKLE2, a scaffolding protein essential for neuroprogenitor division and brain development, revealing interactions with cell division machinery including the APC complex. Analysis of six microcephaly-causing ANKLE2 variants shows how these mutations disrupt the interactome, and molecular dynamics simulations provide mechanistic insight into the resulting dysfunction.

papers.title: MHC restriction is structurally encoded by the T cell receptor germline.
papers.abstract: MHC restriction - the requirement for αβ T cell receptors (TCRs) to recognize Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecules when presenting peptide antigens - is a pillar of adaptive immunity. Here, we provide direct structural evidence for TCR germline-encoded recognition of MHC molecules irrespective of antigenic peptide. We engineered "germline-like" TCRs to eliminate CDR3 specificity for peptide, and a molecular clamping strategy to trap ultra-low-affinity complexes with peptide-MHC for cryo-EM. We find that germline-like TCR/pMHC docking modes are identical to wild-type T cell receptor
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study provides direct structural evidence that T cell receptors (TCRs) recognize MHC molecules through germline-encoded features, independent of the specific peptide antigen. By engineering 'germline-like' TCRs and using a molecular clamping strategy to stabilize ultra-low-affinity complexes, the authors captured cryo-EM structures showing that germline-like TCR/pMHC docking modes are identical to those of wild-type TCRs. This supports the long-standing hypothesis that MHC restriction is hardwired into the TCR germline.

papers.title: Benchmarking machine learning and molecular dynamics methods for the prediction of the thermophysical properties of organic liquids.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of thermophysical properties is crucial for the rational design of lubricants and cooling fluids. We compile a database of approximately 4700 critically evaluated reference values for the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 unique organic molecules in the C10-C50 range. We use this database to train and benchmark a range of machine learning (ML) architectures and molecular representations. XGBoost models trained on molecular descriptors are consistently among the most accurate across all three target properties. Out-of-distribution tests show that descriptor
papers.summary: The authors compiled a database of ~4,700 critically evaluated reference values for density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 organic molecules (C10–C50) and used it to benchmark machine learning architectures and molecular representations against molecular dynamics methods. XGBoost models trained on molecular descriptors consistently performed best across all three properties, though out-of-distribution tests revealed limitations in extrapolative accuracy.

papers.title: Single-Particle STORM Imaging Quantifies Coating Heterogeneity Among Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles.
papers.abstract: Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CNPs) are a potentially transformative biomimetic targeted-delivery platform, which can engage therapeutic targets through source-cell membrane protein functions or homotypic interactions. However, their therapeutic development is limited by the current inability to accurately resolve membrane coating completeness, and CNP particle-to-particle variation. Here, we introduce a STochastic Optical Reconstruction Microscopy (STORM)-based approach that resolves population composition and quantifies membrane coating coverage at the single-particle level. Applying i
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a STORM super-resolution imaging method to quantify how completely individual cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CNPs) are coated with membrane material, revealing substantial particle-to-particle heterogeneity. This addresses a key bottleneck in the therapeutic development of biomimetic delivery platforms, where coating completeness and consistency are hard to measure.

papers.title: Microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase degrades metformin to limit therapeutic response in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Metformin is a first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, yet therapeutic responses vary widely. Whether gut microbes directly inactivate metformin and limit its efficacy remains unclear. Here, we identify a gut microbial aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase, AdhE, from Eubacterium species enriched in individuals with a low response to metformin. AdhE converts metformin to pharmacologically inactive products, lowering intestinal and systemic drug exposure. Genetic deletion of AdhE or phage-mediated depletion of AdhE-producing Eubacterium hallii MD1 restores metformin exposure and glycemic control in mi
papers.summary: This study identifies a gut microbial enzyme, aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase (AdhE), from Eubacterium species that inactivates metformin by converting it into pharmacologically inactive products, thereby reducing drug exposure and limiting its glucose-lowering efficacy. Deleting AdhE or depleting AdhE-producing E. hallii MD1 via phage restores metformin levels and improves glycemic control in mice. The work establishes a direct microbial mechanism underlying variable metformin response in type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Fixed Nonsynonymous vOka Vaccine Mutations in IE62 drive Varicella-Zoster Virus Attenuation in Human Skin.
papers.abstract: The live, attenuated vaccine for Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV) protects against chickenpox in children and adults. However, the vaccine strain Oka (vOka) establishes latency and may reactivate. The molecular basis of vOka attenuation remains unknown. We investigated whether three high-frequency single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that differentiate vOka from parental strain Oka (pOka) are responsible: S628G and R958G in the immediate-early regulatory protein IE62, and *130R in the membrane protein ORF0. We evaluated how these fixed SNPs mediate the attenuated growth phenotype of VZV and dimi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates the genetic basis of attenuation in the live varicella-zoster virus vaccine strain vOka by testing three fixed nonsynonymous mutations that distinguish it from the parental Oka strain. The authors find that two mutations in the immediate-early regulatory protein IE62 (S628G and R958G) are key drivers of the attenuated growth phenotype in human skin, providing mechanistic insight into how the vaccine virus is weakened.

papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound-protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins.
papers.abstract: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine-learning approach for predicting compound-protein interactions at genome-wide scale by leveraging foundation and language models that incorporate the three-dimensional structures of both compounds and proteins. The method aims to overcome the limitations of 1D and 2D representation-based models, which fail to capture geometric binding-site information critical for accurate CPI prediction.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors developed MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to jointly model enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat). They also built MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat data points, and demonstrated its utility for rational enzyme evolution. This addresses a key bottleneck in biocatalysis where experimental kcat measurement is low-throughput and existing computational methods poorly capture enzyme-reaction interplay.

papers.title: GPCR heteromers: Beyond the monomeric paradigm in neuropsychiatric drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest druggable superfamily of membrane proteins and underlie approximately 35% of all approved medicines. Yet this conventional paradigm leaves a substantial minority of neuropsychiatric patients with incomplete efficacy, treatment resistance, or dose-limiting adverse effects. Converging evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology has dismantled the monomeric model. GPCRs function in vivo as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in brain regions directly implicated in disease, including the
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review challenges the long-held view that GPCRs act as isolated monomers, arguing instead that they function as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in the brain. The authors synthesize structural, biophysical, and pharmacological evidence to show that targeting these heteromers could improve treatments for neuropsychiatric disorders where current drugs fall short.

papers.title: A de novo GABPA Variant in a Patient with Multifocal Cutaneous Vascular Tumors of an Unclassified Entity.
papers.abstract: We investigated the genetic basis of a previously unclassified congenital vascular anomaly in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors. Through genomic analysis, we identified a novel heterozygous de novo germline variant in GA-binding protein-alpha (GABPA), an ETS family transcription factor. Histopathologic evaluation demonstrated capillary-venous lesions lacking glucose transporter 1 expression, distinguishing this entity from common infantile hemangioma. Notably, the tumor vasculature exhibited a prominent alpha-SMA-positive perivascular cell layer, with nuclear localized GABPA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel de novo germline variant in the GABPA transcription factor in a patient with multifocal cutaneous vascular tumors that do not fit any known classification. The tumors lack GLUT1 expression and show a distinct alpha-SMA-positive perivascular layer, distinguishing them from infantile hemangioma. The finding links GABPA dysfunction to a previously unclassified vascular anomaly.

papers.title: Criteria-guided selection of alternative zinc-binding groups of HDAC3 inhibitors using in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are epigenetic enzymes linked to several biological functions and diseases. Class I HDACs (HDAC1-3) share high protein sequence and active site similarity. Hydroxamate-based inhibitors, while highly potent, are non-selective with poor pharmacokinetic profile, prompting exploration of alternative zinc-binding groups. The study applied criteria-guided identification of HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups following structure-based virtual screening, with a prioritisation of HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate interaction wit
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening followed by in vitro testing to identify HDAC3 inhibitors that use alternative zinc-binding groups instead of the conventional hydroxamate, aiming to improve selectivity over other class I HDACs and pharmacokinetic properties. The authors prioritized compounds forming HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate or monodentate zinc coordination. The work provides a criteria-guided framework for developing more selective epigenetic inhibitors.

papers.title: A water-pinning hotspot drives templated tau aggregation.
papers.abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP), achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured sol
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, forms seed-competent fibrils that propagate between cells in tauopathies. The authors identify a single dominant 'water-pinning' hotspot that drives in-register stacking of tau molecules onto fibril seeds, preventing mismatched stacking. This templated aggregation mechanism may explain the prion-like spread of tau pathology.

papers.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.
papers.abstract: Monoterpene synthases (mTSs) are a large family of enzymes, which have promising industrial applications, yet remain difficult to engineer due to complex and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we present a structure-based machine learning (ML) framework that accurately predicts whether a mTS is likely to produce linalool or limonene, chosen as canonical examples of linear and cyclic monoterpene products, respectively. Our approach identifies active site properties, which are used as ML features, enabling functional predictions that go beyond sequence alone. As residue pos
papers.summary: The authors developed a structure-based machine learning framework that predicts whether a monoterpene synthase produces linalool (linear) or limonene (cyclic) by using active-site properties as features rather than sequence alone. This data-driven approach helps overcome the difficulty of engineering these enzymes by linking structural pockets to product outcomes.

papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that combines protein language model sequence embeddings with predicted 3D structural features to identify effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria. By integrating geometric structural signals with sequence semantics, it aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only and structure-only prediction methods, which respectively miss conformational cues and suffer from scarce experimental structures.

papers.title: Integrative bioinformatics analysis of Lianmei granules in diabetic nephropathy: Epidemiological and molecular insights.
papers.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a severe complication of diabetes mellitus, leading to end-stage renal disease and significant morbidity. Current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, highlighting the need for novel treatments. Lianmei granules (LMG) show potential for treating DN, although their mechanisms remain unclear. This study explored DN epidemiology and investigated the active components, targets, and mechanisms of LMG using a comprehensive bioinformatics approach. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis involving 44,090 participants from the National Health and Nutrition E
papers.summary: This study combines epidemiological analysis of 44,090 NHANES participants with network pharmacology and bioinformatics to investigate how Lianmei granules (LMG) might treat diabetic nephropathy. The authors identify active compounds, potential protein targets, and enriched pathways, proposing molecular mechanisms for LMG's therapeutic effects. The work is largely computational and hypothesis-generating, without experimental validation of the predicted mechanisms.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the antifungal protein NFAP2 from Aspergillus fischeri to identify fungus-specific intracellular targets in Candida albicans, including glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase. The authors then apply structure-based drug repurposing to find existing compounds that hit these targets, offering a potentially faster route to new antifungal therapies.

papers.title: The structural context of mutations in proteins predicts their effect on antibiotic resistance.
papers.abstract: In Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a prevalent and deadly pathogen, resistance to antibiotics evolves primarily through non-synonymous mutations in proteins. Sequence-based analyses can uncover the genetic basis of antibiotic resistance, but these methods focus on primary sequence and often neglect other biological signals, such as protein structural information. We hypothesize that integrating the structural context of mutations improves the prediction of effects on function and phenotype. We curate high-confidence structural annotations for the M. tuberculosis proteome from 1350 crystallography
papers.summary: This study integrates protein structural annotations into models predicting how mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis proteins affect antibiotic resistance. By curating high-confidence structural data for the proteome, the authors show that incorporating structural context improves predictions of mutational effects on phenotype compared to sequence-only approaches.

papers.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
papers.abstract: Mechanosensitive channels are central to cellular responses to membrane tension, yet the structural basis of their gating remains incompletely understood. Here, we determine the structures of wild-type and Gly22→Ser (G22S) mutants of MscL from Escherichia coli (EcMscL) by cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) in peptide-based lipid nanodiscs and complement them with solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements in liposomes to capture their dynamics in a native-like membrane environment. The cryo-EM structures reveal a closed conformation, whereas analysis of the low-threshold G2
papers.summary: This study combines cryo-EM and solid-state NMR to determine structures and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from E. coli, including a low-threshold G22S mutant, in lipid nanodiscs and liposomes. The cryo-EM structures capture a closed conformation, while NMR provides complementary information on membrane-embedded dynamics relevant to gating. The work offers a detailed structural and dynamic view of how this channel senses membrane tension.

papers.title: In vivo fate-guided design of efficient delivery systems for PROTACs: from molecular rationales to clinical progress.
papers.abstract: Despite two decades of intensive molecular engineering, the clinical translation of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) remains constrained by a fundamental paradox: high in vitro potency often fails to translate into in vivo efficacy due to poor pharmacokinetics (PK)/pharmacodynamics (PD) profiles and uncontrolled biodistribution. This review departs from conventional narratives centered on potency by introducing a framework focused on drug fate that explicitly connects the absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion (ADME), and tumor targeting of PROTACs with the rational design of
papers.summary: This review argues that the clinical translation of PROTAC degraders is limited less by potency than by poor pharmacokinetics and uncontrolled biodistribution, and proposes a 'drug fate'-guided framework linking ADME properties and tumor targeting to rational delivery system design. It connects molecular design rationales with current clinical progress in the field.

papers.title: Fluorination: A strategy to tune the interactions of molecules and nanoscale systems with biological matter.
papers.abstract: Fluorination has become a key molecular engineering strategy in medicinal chemistry and nanomedicine, enabling the fine tuning of the physicochemical and biological properties of therapeutic molecules and drug delivery systems. The unique characteristics of fluorine, including its small steric footprint, high electronegativity, and exceptional strength of the C-F bond, enhance metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and improve pharmacokinetic profiles. Beyond these well-established effects, fluorination has emerged as a tool for controlling the assembly and biological behavio
papers.summary: This review discusses how fluorination—the incorporation of fluorine atoms into molecules and nanoscale systems—can be used to fine-tune their interactions with biological matter. It highlights how fluorine's unique properties (small size, high electronegativity, strong C-F bonds) improve metabolic stability, modulate lipophilicity and acidity, and enhance pharmacokinetics, while also enabling control over molecular assembly and biological behavior in drug delivery and nanomedicine contexts.

papers.title: Structural basis of serine protease inhibition by antibodies from biased Fab phage-display libraries.
papers.abstract: Biased Fab phage-display libraries were designed to determine whether inhibitory CDR H3 motifs from potent anti-matriptase antibodies could be transferred to target homologous serine proteases. Using reverse-binding and substrate-like H3 motifs from parental clones A11 and E2 as templates, six synthetic libraries with 1010 diversity were constructed. Selection against matriptase identified 16 inhibitors with sub-100 nM potency, representing 100,000-fold improvement over circularized H3 loops alone. Selection against TMPRSS2, a serine protease implicated in viral entry and prostate cancer with
papers.summary: This study engineered biased Fab phage-display libraries to transfer inhibitory CDR H3 motifs from anti-matriptase antibodies to homologous serine proteases. Selection against matriptase yielded 16 sub-100 nM inhibitors, a 100,000-fold potency improvement over circularized H3 loops alone, and selections against TMPRSS2 also produced inhibitors. The work provides a structural and methodological framework for generating potent antibody-based serine protease inhibitors.

papers.title: DyME: An MD-based engine exploiting HTP mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry.
papers.abstract: Protein recognition mimicry is of great interest in the field of molecular bioengineering and rational design, with mutagenesis frequently employed to analyze the effects of altering amino acids involved in molecular recognition. The conformational and energetic effects of such alterations can be investigated in detail with the help of molecular dynamics (MD) methodologies. While existing MD-based computational tools can be used to explore a particular set of mutations at a time, suitable for small-scale studies, high-throughput (HTP) exploration of protein recognition for engineering purposes
papers.summary: DyME is a molecular dynamics-based computational engine designed to enable high-throughput exploration of protein mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry. It addresses the limitation of existing MD tools that can only handle small sets of mutations at a time, allowing larger-scale screening of amino acid alterations and their conformational and energetic effects.

papers.title: Semi-Rational Design of CpNampt Mutants for Enhanced Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) Synthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.abstract: β-Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) serves as a direct precursor of the essential cofactor NAD⁺, playing a crucial role in regulating mitochondrial function and delaying cellular aging. Synthetic biology, with its environmental and economic advantages, has become an important approach for the production of natural medicines, with the optimized design of metabolic pathways at its core. In this study, we focused on the NMN‑consuming pathway mediated by the nma1 and pof1 genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and consequently generated their double‑knockout mutant, DHSX02. Futhermore, a highly efficie
papers.summary: This study engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae to boost production of NMN, a precursor to the anti-aging cofactor NAD+. The authors knocked out two NMN-consuming genes (nma1 and pof1) and used semi-rational design to create improved variants of the CpNampt enzyme, enhancing NMN synthesis in yeast.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, and In Vitro Evaluation of Pinostrobin-Based Hydrazones as Potent α‑Glucosidase Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Twenty-four pinostrobin hydrazone derivatives (TN01-TN24) were synthesized through two continuous steps from pinostrobin, hydrazone, and aldehyde derivatives, well characterized and screened for inhibitory activity against yeast α-glucosidase (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). To further expand the chemical space, a QSAR-guided approach was employed, leading to the identification of four additional candidates (TN25-TN28). Eleven compounds exhibited >80% inhibition at 50 μM, outperforming acarbose, with most displaying IC50 values below 10 μM. Among them, TN27 showed the highest potency with an IC50 o
papers.summary: This study synthesized and screened 28 pinostrobin-based hydrazone derivatives for inhibition of yeast α-glucosidase, an enzyme target relevant to diabetes management. Eleven compounds achieved over 80% inhibition at 50 μM, surpassing the standard drug acarbose, with most having IC50 values below 10 μM. The most potent compound, TN27, was identified through QSAR-guided optimization.

papers.title: Computational Design of Three-Dimensional Nitrogenated Holey Graphene Structures with Phase-Dependent Optoelectronic Properties.
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose and comprehensively characterize two novel three-dimensional nitrogenated holey graphene (3D-NHG) structures, designated as the α and β phases. These architectures are predicted through a computational protocol based on the controlled compression of stacked 2D-NHG monolayers. Their dynamical and structural stabilities are assessed via phonon dispersion calculations and molecular dynamics simulations within the density-functional tight-binding framework. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the α phase is a semiconductor with an indirect HSE06 bandgap of 0
papers.summary: This paper computationally designs two novel three-dimensional nitrogenated holey graphene structures (α and β phases) by compressing stacked 2D monolayers. The α phase is predicted to be a semiconductor with an indirect bandgap, and the two phases exhibit distinct optoelectronic properties. Stability is confirmed via phonon dispersion and molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Integrated In silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Piperine Derivatives as Potential Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance mediated by efflux pump activity represents a major challenge in the treatment of infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Efflux pumps such as NorA and MepA reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute significantly to decreased antibiotic efficacy. In this study, PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, was evaluated as a potential efflux pump inhibitor using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Computational analysis, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Lipinski r
papers.summary: This study evaluates PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, as a potential efflux pump inhibitor against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Using molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro assays, the authors assess its ability to inhibit NorA and MepA efflux pumps that contribute to antibiotic resistance. The work suggests piperine derivatives may serve as adjuvant compounds to restore antibiotic efficacy in resistant infections.

papers.title: The PTPN1/N2 Peptide Inhibitor Achieves Potent, Long-Acting Glycemic Control and Weight-Loss Dual Efficacy in Mice.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity are closely linked metabolic disorders driven by insulin and leptin resistance. Current long-acting therapies capable of addressing both conditions are dominated by incretin-based agents, which primarily achieve efficacy through appetite suppression and are frequently associated with tolerability limitations and metabolic rebound after treatment discontinuation. Alternative strategies that correct underlying signaling defects without suppressing food intake remain lacking. Protein tyrosine phosphatases PTPN1 and PTPN2 act as coordinated intracellular negati
papers.summary: This study reports a peptide inhibitor targeting the protein tyrosine phosphatases PTPN1 and PTPN2 that simultaneously improves blood glucose control and promotes weight loss in mice. Unlike incretin-based drugs that mainly suppress appetite, this inhibitor works by correcting underlying insulin and leptin signaling defects, offering a potentially more durable and better-tolerated dual therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity.

papers.title: ParaEM: Antigen-aware sequence-based paratope prediction with Expectation-Maximization.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of antibody paratopes-the residues contacting the antigen-is vital for understanding antibody-antigen recognition, antibody engineering, and vaccine design. However, structure-based predictors require antibody structural inputs, which are often obtained from experimentally determined antibody-antigen complexes in benchmark settings but are generally unavailable for new sequences. Conversely, sequence-based predictors scale efficiently but remain largely antigen-agnostic, limiting their use of pair-specific antigen context.
papers.summary: ParaEM is a new sequence-based method for predicting antibody paratopes (the residues that contact antigen) that incorporates antigen context, unlike prior sequence-based predictors that are largely antigen-agnostic. It uses an Expectation-Maximization framework to make antigen-aware predictions directly from antibody and antigen sequences, avoiding the need for experimentally determined structures required by structure-based predictors.

papers.title: Rational design of a consensus bothropic metalloproteinase as an immunogen for broadly protective antivenom development.
papers.abstract: Antivenoms remain the only specific therapy for snakebite envenoming. In Bothrops venoms, Snake Venom Metalloproteinases (SVMPs) are abundant and highly diverse toxins responsible for the major local and hemotoxic effects induced by envenoming. However, currently available bothropic antivenoms fail to fully neutralize these effects, frequently resulting in permanent and disabling sequelae in affected patients. Here, we describe a rational approach to improve the SVMP neutralization potential of bothropic antivenoms using a consensus toxin. Forty SVMP sequences belonging to PI, P-II, and P-III
papers.summary: The authors rationally designed a consensus snake venom metalloproteinase (SVMP) based on 40 sequences from Bothrops venoms (PI, P-II, and P-III classes) to serve as a broadly protective immunogen for antivenom development. This consensus toxin aims to overcome the diversity of SVMPs that current bothropic antivenoms fail to fully neutralize, potentially reducing local and hemotoxic sequelae from snakebite envenoming.

papers.title: Ginsenoside Rb1 From the Functional Food Panax ginseng Suppresses Pancreatic Cancer Progression via Macrophage Reprogramming Through the PI3K-AKT Pathway.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly malignant gastrointestinal tumor, and its nutritional intervention strategies remain relatively limited. Ginseng, a representative medicinal herb officially included in China's "Food and Medicinal Same Origin" catalogue, is widely used in tea beverages, soups, and functional foods. Its active component, ginsenoside Rb1 (GRB1), derived from the medicine-food homology plant Panax ginseng, has been reported to possess antitumor and immunomodulatory effects, but its role in the PDAC tumor microenvironment remains unclear. This study aims to scree
papers.summary: This study investigates whether ginsenoside Rb1, a compound from the food-medicine plant Panax ginseng, can suppress pancreatic cancer progression by reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages. The authors report that GRB1 acts through the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway to alter macrophage behavior and inhibit PDAC growth, suggesting a potential nutritional intervention strategy for this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: SMartini: automated small molecule parametrization for Martini 3 force field.
papers.abstract: We present SMartini, an automated pipeline for deriving Martini 3 coarse-grained force-field parameters for arbitrary small molecules. Starting from a molecular structure or a SMILES string, the pipeline maps the all-atom molecule onto a coarse-grained bead representation and automatically fits both bonded and non-bonded parameters. Bonded parameters are obtained via Boltzmann inversion of atomistic molecular dynamics trajectories; successive rounds of coarse-grained simulation and distribution-matching updates then refine these estimates until the coarse-grained conformational ensemble reprod
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SMartini is an automated pipeline that generates Martini 3 coarse-grained force-field parameters for arbitrary small molecules directly from a structure or SMILES string. It maps the all-atom molecule onto beads and fits bonded parameters via Boltzmann inversion of atomistic MD trajectories, then iteratively refines them through coarse-grained simulation and distribution matching. This lowers the barrier to coarse-grained simulation of small molecules by removing manual parametrization.

papers.title: Systematic exploration of predicted quaternary structures within pandemic-relevant viral proteomes.
papers.abstract: Mechanistic understanding of viral protein-protein interactions enables global health security and pandemic preparedness, yet experimental characterisation remains difficult, costly, and often restricted to specialised laboratories. Here, we describe an in silico campaign using AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold-Multimer to predict monomers and dimer structures within 2,812 viral proteomes from 23 viral families relevant to human health. We report high-confidence predicted structures of 5,279 hetero-, and 2,749 homo-dimers. Structural clustering of interfaces reduces the set fivefold to 1,598 consolidat
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold-Multimer to predict monomer and dimer structures across 2,812 viral proteomes from 23 human-relevant viral families, generating high-confidence models for thousands of hetero- and homo-dimers. Structural clustering of interfaces consolidated the set fivefold, providing a large-scale resource of predicted viral quaternary structures to support pandemic preparedness and mechanistic studies of viral protein-protein interactions.

papers.title: UHPLC/MS-MS Profiling, Antioxidant and Antimicrobial Properties of Atriplex halimus L. and Marrubium deserti De Noé Extracts: In Vitro and In Silico.
papers.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the chemical composition and both in vitro and in silico antioxidant and antimicrobial activities of Atriplex halimus L. and Marrubium deserti De Noé, collected from Algeria. UHPLC‑MS/MS analysis revealed that the major compounds in the tested extracts are protocatechuic aldehyde, caffeic acid, cynaroside, and cosmosiin. The data demonstrated that the dichloromethane fraction was richer in polyphenols and flavonoids than the aqueous fraction. The extracts exhibited greater antioxidant capacity against ABTS compared to DPPH and FRAP assays. Antimicrobial activity was
papers.summary: This study profiles the chemical composition of Atriplex halimus and Marrubium deserti extracts using UHPLC-MS/MS, identifying major polyphenols such as protocatechuic aldehyde, caffeic acid, cynaroside, and cosmosiin. The dichloromethane fractions were richer in polyphenols and flavonoids and showed stronger antioxidant activity against ABTS than DPPH or FRAP, alongside antimicrobial effects supported by in silico analyses.

papers.title: Phytochemical Fingerprinting of Sanchezia nobilis Hook. F. Leaf Extract and Evaluation of Anxiolytic, Cytotoxic, and Antioxidant Activities In Vivo, In Vitro, and In Silico.
papers.abstract: Present studies emphasize the pharmacological, toxicological, and molecular simulation studies of the potent phytoconstituents in the Sanchezia nobilis leaf extract (SNE) and its nonpolar and polar fractions. We identified 27 phytoconstituents in SNE using Gas Chromatography Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS), where aniline, dibutyl phthalate, and isoquinoline are noteworthy. Anxiolytic assessments by hole board test (HBT) and elevated plus maze test (EPMT) demonstrated dose-dependent effects of nonpolar and polar fractions of SNE. Both fractions also exhibited minimal cytotoxicity in brine shrimp leth
papers.summary: This study profiles 27 phytochemicals in Sanchezia nobilis leaf extract via GC-MS and tests its fractions for anxiolytic, cytotoxic, and antioxidant activities using in vivo, in vitro, and in silico approaches. The nonpolar and polar fractions showed dose-dependent anxiolytic effects and minimal brine shrimp cytotoxicity, with molecular simulations supporting the bioactivity of key constituents.

papers.title: Chlorothiophene-Substituted N-Phenylpyrazolines: Synthesis, Anticancer Evaluation, and Computational Insight into COX-2 Inhibition.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for novel anticancer agents. Pyrazoline derivatives have attracted considerable interest due to their structural flexibility, enabling modifications, including bioisosteric replacement, to enhance anticancer potential. In this study, eight N-phenylpyrazoline analogs bearing chlorothiophene moieties were synthesized via cyclocondensation of chalcone intermediates with phenylhydrazine, yielding 59%-94%. Structural characterization was confirmed using ATR-IR, GC-MS, 1H-, and 13C-NMR analyses. The synthesized derivatives
papers.summary: This study synthesized eight chlorothiophene-substituted N-phenylpyrazoline compounds and tested their anticancer activity, with structural confirmation via IR, GC-MS, and NMR. Computational docking analysis suggests these compounds may inhibit COX-2, pointing to a possible mechanism for their anticancer effects. The work represents early-stage medicinal chemistry exploring pyrazoline scaffolds as potential anticancer agents.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology-Based Prediction and In Vivo Validation of Fumonisin B1-Induced Liver Injury and Early Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Fumonisin B1 (FB1) is a widespread mycotoxin contaminating food and feed, exhibiting severe hepatotoxicity. This study aimed to systematically investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms of FB1-induced liver injury and early liver fibrosis by combining network pharmacology with an in vivo animal model. First, network pharmacology and molecular docking were utilized to screen the core targets and key signaling pathways of FB1-induced hepatotoxicity. Subsequently, an in vivo C57BL/6 mouse model was established via intragastric administration of FB1 (5 mg/kg/day for 28 days). Serum levels of
papers.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
papers.summary: This study combines network pharmacology and molecular docking with an in vivo mouse model to identify core targets and signaling pathways underlying fumonisin B1-induced liver injury and early fibrosis. The authors validate their computational predictions experimentally, showing that FB1 exposure (5 mg/kg/day for 28 days) causes hepatotoxicity and early fibrotic changes in C57BL/6 mice.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify potential PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is an anticancer target, and the work highlights marine compounds as a promising source for new inhibitor scaffolds.

papers.title: Trypsinogen Pro-Region as a Molecular Scaffold for the Design of Competitive Peptide Inhibitors of Trypsin-Like Proteases.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. Merrill) productivity is severely impacted by the velvetbean caterpillar Anticarsia gemmatalis Hübner, 1818 (Lepidoptera: Erebidae), a major defoliating pest in soybean-producing regions. Current management strategies rely heavily on chemical insecticides, which are associated with environmental risks and the development of resistance. Protease inhibitors have emerged as a promising alternative, as protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae is primarily mediated by trypsin-like serine proteases. In this context, the rational design of short inhibitory peptides represents
papers.journal: Archives of insect biochemistry and physiology
papers.summary: This paper explores using the pro-region of trypsinogen as a molecular scaffold to rationally design short competitive peptide inhibitors targeting trypsin-like serine proteases in the velvetbean caterpillar, a major soybean pest. The goal is to develop eco-friendly alternatives to chemical insecticides by disrupting protein digestion in lepidopteran larvae.

papers.title: Multidimensional molecular profiling reveals decidual and circulating NK cell dynamics in early and late pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Human pregnancy presents a unique physiological state that allows for growth of an antigenically dissimilar foetus. The immune system plays a key role in establishing and maintaining successful pregnancy, yet detailed understanding of immunological responses in pregnancy is lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses multidimensional molecular profiling to characterize natural killer (NK) cell populations in both the decidua (uterine lining) and peripheral blood across early and late pregnancy. It reveals dynamic changes in NK cell phenotypes and molecular states that may support immune tolerance of the fetus. The findings provide a detailed resource for understanding how NK cells adapt during pregnancy.

papers.title: Identification of Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 with potential relevance to prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Glutathione S-transferase Pi 1 (GSTP1) is frequently silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD), yet whether its residual catalytic activity can be chemically enhanced is largely unexplored. Here, we identify Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 through structure-based screening, biophysical characterisation, and biochemical validation. Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) supported a concentration-dependent association between Crocin I and GSTP1, and enzymatic assays demonstrated enhanced catalytic activity. Michaelis-Menten kinetics showed that Crocin I increased Vmax without markedly alterin
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study identifies Crocin I, a natural compound, as a positive modulator that binds GSTP1 and enhances its catalytic activity, as shown by biophysical binding assays and enzyme kinetics. Since GSTP1 is often silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma, chemically boosting residual enzyme activity could offer a new therapeutic angle for prostate cancer.

papers.title: Molecular biophysics of viral proteins: From mechanistic insights to microbiological and clinical applications.
papers.abstract: Viral proteins are dynamic molecular machines that couple molecular-scale events to microbiological phenotypes, including host-cell tropism, entry efficiency, environmental persistence, strain-specific immune escape, and antiviral resistance. In this review, we critically evaluated how experimental, computational, and biochemical approaches define these links and support clinical translation. We organized the evidence around four key observables: Structure, dynamics, mechanics, and thermodynamics. We then assessed which conclusions remained robust across methods and viral families. Nuclear mag
papers.summary: This review examines how experimental, computational, and biochemical methods reveal the structure, dynamics, mechanics, and thermodynamics of viral proteins, linking molecular-scale behavior to phenotypes such as host tropism, immune escape, and antiviral resistance. It assesses which mechanistic conclusions hold across different methods and viral families and how these insights can support clinical translation.

papers.title: Tau protein in Parkinson's disease: advances in phosphoproteomics and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Tau dysregulation, particularly abnormal phosphorylation, is increasingly implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD) and in the pathogenic interaction between Tau and α-synuclein. This review proposes an integrated PD-focused workflow connecting phosphoproteomic discovery, structural modeling, computational drug discovery, and experimental validation. Phosphoproteomic analyses of post-mortem brain tissue, biofluids, and patient-derived dopaminergic neuronal models can identify candidate Tau phosphosignatures associated with vulnerable brain regions, α-synuclein pathology, genetic background, or cl
papers.summary: This review proposes an integrated workflow for studying Tau dysregulation in Parkinson's disease, linking phosphoproteomic discovery in brain tissue, biofluids, and patient-derived neurons with structural modeling, computational drug discovery, and experimental validation. It highlights how Tau phosphosignatures may relate to vulnerable brain regions, α-synuclein pathology, and genetic background, aiming to bridge multi-omics and simulation approaches for PD research.

papers.title: Shared immune perturbations in hepatocellular carcinoma-depression comorbidity and synergistic immunotherapeutic effects of fluoxetine combined with anti-PD-1.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often coexists with depression, elevating patient mortality by 39%. The tryptophan metabolic axis bridges tumor and neuropsychiatric immune dysfunction, yet the immunometabolic crosstalk underlying HCC-depression comorbidity remains poorly defined, and reliable combinatorial immunotherapies are absent.
papers.summary: This study investigates the shared immune and metabolic perturbations linking hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and depression, focusing on the tryptophan metabolic axis as a bridge between tumor and neuropsychiatric immune dysfunction. The authors report that combining the antidepressant fluoxetine with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy produces synergistic anti-tumor effects, suggesting a potential combinatorial treatment strategy for patients with HCC-depression comorbidity.

papers.title: Insights into osteoporosis triggered by common antiepileptic drugs via network toxicology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Antiepileptic drugs (AEDs), first-line treatments for epilepsy and related seizure disorders, are increasingly recognized as important risk factors for osteoporosis. However, the molecular mechanisms and specific targets underlying AED-induced bone loss remain largely unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology combined with molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how common antiepileptic drugs may trigger osteoporosis. The authors identify potential molecular targets and pathways linking AED exposure to bone loss, offering mechanistic hypotheses for a known clinical side effect.

papers.title: Reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics-driven design of a multiepitope vaccine candidate against Renibacterium salmoninarum.
papers.abstract: Renibacterium salmoninarum, the etiological agent of bacterial kidney disease (BKD), remains a major challenge for salmonid aquaculture due to its intracellular lifestyle, chronic infection pattern, and the limited efficacy of current control strategies. In this study, a multiepitope vaccine candidate against Renibacterium salmoninarum was designed using reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics approaches. Conserved antigenic proteins shared among three bacterial strains were identified through a systematic screening pipeline that included virulence prediction, essentiality analysis, antigeni
papers.summary: This study used reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics to design a multiepitope vaccine candidate against Renibacterium salmoninarum, the bacterium causing bacterial kidney disease in salmonids. The authors screened conserved antigenic proteins across three bacterial strains, applying virulence prediction, essentiality analysis, and antigenicity assessment to identify promising epitopes for vaccine construction. The work provides an in silico vaccine design that could offer a new strategy for controlling this economically important aquaculture pathogen.

papers.title: Multimodal profiling uncovers an aging-associated ETS1-MYO1B vascular niche responsive to ipragliflozin.
papers.abstract: Tissue aging involves complex changes in vascular, immune, and stromal compartments that collectively reshape the local tissue ecosystem and may contribute to age-related diseases, including cancer, fibrotic diseases, and cardiovascular disease. However, it remains unclear whether reproducible, cell-specific vascular niche states emerge during aging and whether these states can be therapeutically targeted.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Using multimodal profiling, the authors identify a reproducible aging-associated vascular niche state marked by ETS1-MYO1B expression that emerges across tissues during aging. This niche can be targeted pharmacologically, as the SGLT2 inhibitor ipragliflozin modulates it, suggesting a potential therapeutic avenue for age-related vascular dysfunction.

papers.title: Integrated computational investigation of Glycosmis pentaphylla-derived compounds against major venom proteins of Daboia russelii.
papers.abstract: Snakebite envenomation remains a significant neglected tropical disease, particularly in South Asia, where Daboia russelii (Russell's viper) causes substantial morbidity and mortality. Current antivenom therapy is limited by poor efficacy against local tissue damage, high production costs, restricted toxin specificity, and adverse immune reactions, highlighting the need for alternative or adjunct therapeutic strategies. Using an integrated computational and experimental approach, phytocompounds identified from Glycosmis pentaphylla leaf extracts were evaluated as potential inhibitors of major
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and simulation to screen phytocompounds from Glycosmis pentaphylla leaf extracts as potential inhibitors of major venom proteins from Russell's viper (Daboia russelii), a leading cause of snakebite morbidity in South Asia. The work aims to identify plant-derived alternatives or adjuncts to conventional antivenom, which has limited efficacy against local tissue damage and carries cost and immune-reaction drawbacks.

papers.title: Discovery of sunflower-derived umami peptides via machine learning and molecular dynamics simulation of their interactions with the T1R1/T1R3 receptor.
papers.abstract: Umami recognition relies on T1R1/T1R3 binding with umami peptides, but the interaction mechanisms remain unclear. This study aims to reveal the taste mechanisms of four potential umami peptides at both sensory and molecular levels.
papers.summary: This study identifies four potential umami peptides derived from sunflower by combining machine learning prediction with molecular dynamics simulations of their binding to the T1R1/T1R3 umami receptor. It provides molecular-level insight into how these peptides interact with the receptor, linking computational predictions to sensory taste mechanisms.

papers.title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore ana
papers.summary: This study uses a 3D CNN-CVAE combined with LSTM-based molecular generation to design novel rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors for restless legs syndrome. Fourteen unique candidates were generated and screened via pocket prediction, docking, interaction profiling, and pharmacophore analysis. The work demonstrates a generative deep learning pipeline for structure-guided drug design in a neurological context.

papers.title: Identification of flavonoids from natural products against hyperlipidaemia through computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Over the centuries, hyperlipidaemia has been recognised as a major risk factor contributing to cardiovascular disease (CVD). Current research increasingly explores natural compounds such as flavonoids for their potential lipid-lowering effects. This study evaluated pharmacological potential of flavonoids to identify strong inhibitors for target receptor, Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type (PCSK9). A total of 29 compounds, including one FDA-approved drugs were screened for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, followed by molecular docking and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using PC
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 29 flavonoids and one FDA-approved drug for their ability to inhibit PCSK9, a key cholesterol-regulating protein target for hyperlipidaemia. Using drug-likeness filters, ADMET predictions, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors identified promising flavonoid candidates with favorable binding and pharmacokinetic profiles. The work provides a computational foundation for developing natural-product-based PCSK9 inhibitors, though experimental validation is still needed.

papers.title: A dual-functional antiviral and anticancer peptide to target intricate host-pathogen interacting proteins of human papillomavirus associated with head and neck cancer.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is increasingly being reported worldwide, and a major contributing factor is the incidence of human papillomavirus infections. The viral infection activates proto-oncogenes and signalling mechanisms aiding in tumorigenesis. An efficient way to block the virus-induced carcinogenesis is to identify a common medicament that can effectively inhibit the viral and host proteins. In the present study, HNSCC transcriptomic profiles and HPV genes involved in host-pathogen interactions were retrieved. The overexpressed HNSCC genes were further considered for host-pa
papers.summary: The authors used transcriptomic data from head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and HPV to identify host and viral proteins involved in host-pathogen interactions, then designed a dual-functional peptide intended to inhibit both viral and host targets. This computational/peptide-design approach aims to block HPV-driven carcinogenesis by hitting a shared interaction node, though experimental validation appears limited in the abstract.

papers.title: An immunoinformatics-driven multiepitope subunit vaccine targeting Oropouche virus: Molecular docking, immune and dynamics simulation approaches.
papers.abstract: The Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging zoonotic orthobunyavirus responsible for recurring outbreaks of febrile illness and neurological disorders in South and Central America. Despite its growing public health issues, no FDA-approved vaccines or antiviral therapies currently exist. To address this gap, a multiepitope subunit vaccine was designed to target OROV glycoproteins G1 (Gn), G2 (Gc), and the nucleocapsid (N) protein using a reverse-vaccinology (RV) approach. For vaccine construction, suitable epitopes (MHC-I, MHC-II, and linear B-cell) were selected based on percentile rank, antigen
papers.summary: This study used reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics to design a multiepitope subunit vaccine targeting the Oropouche virus, combining MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell epitopes from the viral glycoproteins G1, G2, and nucleocapsid protein. Molecular docking and immune/dynamics simulations were used to predict that the construct binds stably to immune receptors and could elicit both humoral and cellular responses. The work is entirely computational, so experimental validation is still needed before any clinical relevance.

papers.title: Underpinning hierarchical anisotropic structure formation in soy protein high-moisture extrudates by Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
papers.abstract: Plant-based meat alternatives are fibrous anisotropic food protein products that mimic the texture and palatability of animal-based foods. The main industrially scalable production technique for manufacturing such structured protein materials is high-moisture extrusion, which involves the thermo-mechanical processing, and subsequent cooling, of a hot protein melt in the presence of shear and temperature gradients. Yet, the complex mechanisms governing fibrous structure formation in plant-protein extrudates are poorly characterised, in turn limiting the rational design and optimisation of the e
papers.summary: This study uses Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) to visualize how hierarchical anisotropic (directionally aligned) structures form inside soy protein high-moisture extrudates during processing. The work links thermo-mechanical processing conditions and shear/temperature gradients to the fibrous texture of plant-based meat analogues, providing structural insight that could guide rational design of these products.

papers.title: Nanozymes in Tumor Microenvironment Modulation for Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central regulatory role in malignant tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, and its complexity and dynamic heterogeneity markedly limit the efficacy of current treatment strategies. Therefore, the development of novel functional materials capable of effectively remodeling the TME and alleviating immunosuppression and therapeutic tolerance has become an important research direction in cancer therapy. In recent years, nanozymes, as a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity, have shown broad potential in TME intervention and
papers.summary: This review discusses how nanozymes—nanomaterials that mimic natural enzyme catalytic activity—can be used to remodel the tumor microenvironment and overcome therapeutic resistance in cancer. It highlights the potential of these materials to alleviate immunosuppression and improve treatment outcomes by targeting the complex, dynamic TME.

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies ethyl rosmarinate as a SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: SLC1A6 remains poorly characterized in bladder cancer. This study investigated its expression pattern, clinical relevance, cellular localization, functional implications, and potential pharmacological modulation.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the poorly understood glutamate transporter SLC1A6 in bladder cancer, examining its expression, clinical relevance, and cellular function. Using structure-based virtual screening, the authors identify ethyl rosmarinate as a candidate compound targeting SLC1A6, proposing it as a potential therapeutic for bladder cancer.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme for viral DNA replication, to identify potential antiviral drug candidates. The screen focused on FDA-approved compounds, aiming to find rapidly repurposable drugs for mpox treatment, which currently lacks targeted therapies.
